W4 after E007. Results: E005 (SGD+EMA, 9 ep) 0.7583 at 9.10 s. E006 (Muon, bs2000, EMA) 0.7649 at 9.45 s. E007 (Muon+EMA+progressive resize 24/28/32) 0.7590 at 7.33 s. That is the best feasible run, and it is 19% faster than E006 for a 0.6 pp accuracy loss.

Beliefs:
1. Time scales with pixel count and epoch count. Resizing saved about 2.1 s, more than my 1 s guess. I missed on both time and accuracy, so my skeptic prior is too pessimistic about systems gains here. Compute dominates, and the compile/eager overhead is small. Per-epoch cost is now about 0.8 s, with fixed cost of roughly 0.3-0.5 s.
2. Accuracy gains from EMA (+1 pp) and Muon (+0.6 pp) were real and larger than I expected. Resizing cost about 0.6 pp, less than I feared.
3. Noise. Compiled runs are near-deterministic per seed, so re-running the same recipe gives almost the same result. Changing the recipe reshuffles the trajectory. The 3-seed mean std from recipe changes is about 0.15-0.25 pp. Time noise is about 1-2%, or 0.1 s. The 40-seed mean is likely 0.1-0.3 pp below the 3-seed mean, so 0.759 is thin against the 0.75 judgment bar, though it is above the 0.753 local bar.
4. The slope is about 0.3-0.6 pp per 0.5 epoch. Cutting to 8.5 epochs would likely drop accuracy to about 0.754-0.756 and save about 5% of time. That is a coin flip on feasibility.
5. Regression: gains from lucky seeds regress. Most small tweaks (width 512, LR floor, BN recompute) are within noise. Aggressive resizing (20 px) likely costs accuracy below the bar.

Unsure: the true 40-seed mean, whether the LR-to-0 change helps with EMA, whether CUDA graphs help under the 4-CPU pin (Muon with its compiled updates may already be launch-bound), and the first-epoch overhead.

forecasts.reason: Fewer epochs saves about 5% of time and costs about 0.35 pp, which leaves accuracy near the 0.753 bar.
Zero-floor LR with EMA gives a small gain of about 0.1-0.2 pp, within noise.
Spending 30% of steps at 20 px saves about 10% of time but likely costs 0.8 pp, which puts accuracy below the bar.
The saving is about 3% of time and the accuracy loss is about 0.2 pp, which is near the noise.
The held-out mean regresses by about 0.1-0.3 pp from 0.759, and the per-seed std is about 0.3 pp.
Graph capture with Muon and several resolutions is risky and the saving is probably small, since compute dominates.
The Lookahead/EMA BN buffers are already averaged, so recomputing them gives about 0.05 pp, below the 0.3 pp bar.

cruxes: What is the 40-seed mean accuracy of E007, and what is the per-seed std? That decides how many epochs can be cut.
Is the train step launch-bound under the 4-CPU pin, which would make CUDA graphs a big win, or compute-bound, which would make them small?
How much of the time is fixed cost (data transfer, whitening, first-step warm-up) versus per-epoch cost?
